prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a counter environment where a bearded man in a hoodie stands in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres, shifting across the visual field from left-of-centre in frame 1 to the far right in frame 5 as the camera wearer turns left. To the right of the man (frames 1–4) sits a glass pastry display case about 1.2 to 1.8 metres away and a red shopping basket in the lower right foreground within arm's reach (under 0.8 metres), while frames 4 and 5 reveal a brown paper bag on the counter (~0.9 metres away) and a wire snack rack to its left (~1.2 metres away) with a deep background hallway extending beyond 4 metres behind them. Across the five frames, the man's right arm extends forward in frames 1–2 and his hands come together at waist level in frame 5 within his own arm's reach, while the lower counter, basket, and parts of his lower torso are partly cut off at the bottom frame edge. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the foreground paper bag, snack rack, and man from the dark background corridor and back wall, making relative distances across the counter immediately apparent. However, the map is unreliable in frame 4 where the man's torso is rendered anomalously dark (farther) compared to the brighter paper bag beside him, and in frame 5 where the wire snack rack's open grid is filled in as a solid planar surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the primary standing man in pink ('person') in the foreground (~0.8–1.2 metres away) across all five frames as his relative position shifts from the left side in frame 1 to the right side in frame 5, while also detecting a distant background person (~4–5 metres away in the hallway to the left of him) in frames 3 and 5. To the right of the main man in frames 1–4, the glass display case (~1.2–1.8 metres away) is segmented as a boxy region, while the lower edge of frame 1 captures a small foreground object below the case and frame 4 segments part of the brown paper bag on the left (~0.9 metres away, ~0.4 metres from the man's right arm). The man faces generally toward the camera wearer with his head tilted downward toward the counter rather than looking directly into the lens, and his lower body is occluded by the bottom edge of the frame and the counter. This map highlights the small, distant person standing in the background hallway in frames 3 and 5 who is easily overlooked against the cluttered RGB background. However, the segmentation is unreliable in its class labels and completeness: it mislabels the pastry display case as 'tv', the man's hoodie string/lapel as 'tie' (frame 2), the paper bag top as 'bottle' (frame 4), and splits the man's hands and lower arms into a separate 'person' instance in frame 5 while completely missing the foreground snack rack, red basket, and counter.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the foreground man standing ~0.8 to 1.2 metres in front of the camera wearer, capturing his torso, arms, facial landmarks, and hands only in frames 2, 4, and 5. In all detected frames, the symmetrical arrangement of his shoulders and the downward placement of his nose and eye keypoints relative to his ears confirm his torso faces the camera wearer while his head is pitched downward toward the counter surface rather than looking at the camera. In frame 2 only his upper shoulders, elbows, and facial points are plotted near the left-centre; in frame 4 his full torso and both arms are shown extending downward with his right hand (magenta) hovering at counter height within arm's reach of the paper bag to the left and his left wrist reaching the bottom edge; and in frame 5, positioned on the right, both elbows bend inward to bring his left and right magenta hand skeletons together at waist level. Unlike the RGB image, where dark clothing and motion blur obscure exact joint locations in frame 4, the pose map explicitly localizes his shoulder-hip torso box and finger articulations. However, the pose estimation is highly unreliable across time, completely failing to detect the foreground man in frames 1 and 3, missing the distant background person entirely across all frames, and hallucinating short vertical leg segments directly beneath his waist in frame 4 where his lower body is actually occluded by the counter.
